ai-at-work.title: Forcepoint details TeamPCP supply chain attack that turned LiteLLM into a credential stealer
ai-at-work.excerpt: A new report out today from cybersecurity company Forcepoint LLC’s X-Labs research team details a supply chain attack that compromised LiteLLM, a widely used open-source Python library that serves as
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Forcepoint researchers discovered that LiteLLM, a popular open-source library used by thousands of developers to access AI models, was compromised in a supply chain attack that weaponized it as a credential stealer. This matters because it shows how a single trusted dependency can become a backdoor into your entire cloud and AI infrastructure if you're not actively monitoring what your teams are pulling in. The real kicker is that this happened to a library specifically designed to abstract away complexity, which means people trusted it more than they probably should have without actually checking what it was doing.

ai-at-work.title: Multiplayer AI startup Dust raises $40M to help enterprises move beyond isolated AI assistants
ai-at-work.excerpt: Dust, an agentic artificial intelligence startup that’s trying to push enterprise workers away from isolated chatbots into a more collaborative, multiplayer ecosystem, said today it has raised $40 mil
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Dust just raised $40 million to build collaborative AI systems that let multiple AI assistants work together instead of you bouncing between separate chatbots. This matters because your workers are already drowning in point solutions, and fragmented AI tools only make that worse. The real question is whether enterprises actually want multiplayer AI coordination or if we're just adding another layer of complexity to an already messy tech stack.

ai-at-work.title: The big tent: Dell’s expanding partnerships demonstrate strategic shift in enterprise infrastructure
ai-at-work.excerpt: A significant reorganization is currently taking place within the enterprise infrastructure market, which means that Dell Technologies Inc. will play a prominent role in the outcome. To be successful,
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Dell is doubling down on partnerships across enterprise infrastructure and AI instead of trying to own everything themselves, which represents a meaningful shift from their traditional approach. This matters because digital workplace teams now need to understand that their infrastructure vendors will increasingly depend on partner ecosystems, which could affect everything from support models to integration complexity. Here's the thing though: partnerships sound great until you're the one trying to get three different vendors to actually work together when something breaks at 2 AM.

ai-at-work.title: GridCare raises $64M to speed up AI data center projects
ai-at-work.excerpt: GridCare Inc., a startup that helps data center operators more quickly connect their facilities to the electrical grid, has raised $64 million in funding. Early Nvidia Corp. backer Sutter Hill Venture
ai-at-work.dwp_take: GridCare just raised 64 million dollars to help data centers connect to the power grid faster, which matters because AI infrastructure is eating electricity like never before and grid delays are becoming a real bottleneck. For digital workplace folks, this translates to the backends supporting your cloud services and AI tools actually being able to scale without waiting around for power infrastructure to catch up. The whole thing is basically venture capital's way of admitting that Moore's Law died but the power bill didn't get the memo.

tools-tech.title: I switched to a Bose-Sonos hybrid setup for my home audio - and it worked harmoniously
tools-tech.excerpt: Months after sunsetting the SoundTouch lineup, Bose's Lifestyle Ultra proves that it can still make versatile and great-sounding speaker.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Bose is bringing its premium audio systems back into the game with a new product that plays nicely with Sonos ecosystems, proving the company hasn't completely abandoned the home audio space. This matters because your employees are spending more time in hybrid work setups, and audio quality during video calls and focused work sessions directly impacts productivity and fatigue. Honestly, if Bose can figure out ecosystem compatibility better than most software vendors manage to do with their own products, maybe there's hope for enterprise collaboration tools yet.

tools-tech.title: 5 ways to curb AI sprawl without stifling innovation
tools-tech.excerpt: The trend shows no sign of slowing. McKinsey’s latest The State of AI report suggests that 88% of organizations now use AI in at least one business function. As adoption expands, so too will experimen
tools-tech.dwp_take: Most organizations are now using AI somewhere, but a lot of that experimentation is happening outside formal IT oversight, which creates the sprawl problem. This matters because unmanaged AI tools breed security gaps, duplicate spending, and integration nightmares that eventually land on the IT team's desk anyway. The real trick isn't stopping people from using AI, it's making it easier for them to use approved tools than to sneak around you, which is way harder than it sounds but necessary.

tools-tech.title: How Southwest Airlines is putting endpoint operations on autopilot
tools-tech.excerpt: As digital tools become more central to its operations, Southwest Airlines is increasingly turning to AI and automation to prevent endpoint issues from affecting the sprawling airline. The new tools a
tools-tech.dwp_take: Southwest Airlines is using AI and automation to proactively manage endpoint issues instead of constantly fighting fires after they happen. This matters because most digital workplace teams are drowning in reactive work, so seeing a large organization actually shift to prevention instead of panic-mode troubleshooting is worth paying attention to. The real question is whether Southwest's IT team will actually stay strategic or if they'll just fill those freed-up hours with new projects until they're reactive again anyway.

digital-culture.title: Mozilla’s Mark Surman on 3 ways CEOs can build trust in AI
digital-culture.excerpt: Hello and welcome to Modern CEO! I’m Stephanie Mehta, CEO and chief content officer of Mansueto Ventures. Each week this newsletter explores inclusive approaches to leadership drawn from conversations
digital-culture.dwp_take: Mark Surman from Mozilla is apparently telling CEOs that trust in AI requires transparency, accountability, and getting employees involved in how AI gets deployed. This matters to digital workplace folks because employees are the ones actually living with AI tools every day, and their buy-in determines whether your new AI implementation becomes a real productivity win or a shelf-ware disaster. Here's the thing though: most of this boils down to just doing the basics right, which somehow still feels revolutionary in a world where executives want to deploy AI before anyone understands what it actually does.

digital-culture.title: We don’t have a burnout epidemic. We have a burnout buzzword problem
digital-culture.excerpt: One cold Friday night a few years ago, I collapsed to the ground in the arrivals hall of a small French airport. I started sobbing and couldn’t stop. It took physical collapse for me to acknowledge th
digital-culture.dwp_take: The article argues that "burnout" has become so overused as a catch-all term that we've lost sight of actual, serious burnout and what causes it. This matters to digital workplace folks because we're often blamed for burnout (endless Slack notifications, always-on culture) when the real culprit is usually unsustainable workloads and bad management. Here's the thing though: telling people their burnout is just a buzzword doesn't fix the fact that they're still exhausted, so maybe we focus less on semantics and more on actually changing how work gets done.

digital-culture.title: How to balance your passion and your day job
digital-culture.excerpt: It’s graduation season and my email inbox is flooded with inquiries from students entering the workforce, looking for career advice. How do I land my dream job? What should I do at the company where I
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece is offering career advice to new graduates about balancing their passion projects with their actual jobs. This matters to digital workplace leaders because employees who feel trapped between their real work and their dreams tend to disengage, skip meetings, and eventually leave. My take: stop hiring people based on their "passion" and instead build jobs that don't feel like a holding pattern before their real life starts.

digital-culture.title: Stop selling what you think your customers need and start doing this instead
digital-culture.excerpt: I used to think I was a great salesperson because I had all the right answers. I knew my product inside and out. I could explain every feature, every benefit, every reason someone should say yes. And
digital-culture.dwp_take: This article is basically saying stop pitching features and start listening to what customers actually need instead. For digital workplace pros, this is critical because we've spent years jamming collaboration tools and platforms at people without first understanding their real problems or workflows. The irony is that most failed digital workplace transformations happened because someone fell in love with a solution before they bothered asking employees what was actually broken.

industry-news.title: Modernizing commute benefits for today’s flexible workforce
industry-news.excerpt: With hybrid work reshaping commutes, flexible benefits help employees return with ease.
industry-news.dwp_take: Companies are reworking commute benefits to fit hybrid and flexible work arrangements instead of assuming everyone shows up five days a week. This matters because your digital workplace strategy only works if employees can actually get to the office when they need to, and outdated transit subsidies alienate remote and hybrid workers who rarely use them. Here's the thing: stop treating commute benefits like they're set in stone from 1995, and you'll actually retain people instead of watching them resent you for benefits they can't use.

industry-news.title: AI readiness is no longer optional for leadership teams
industry-news.excerpt: AI adoption is accelerating, but many organizations are not ready to scale it responsibly.
industry-news.dwp_take: Leadership teams across most organizations still lack the skills and frameworks to implement AI at scale without creating chaos. This matters because digital workplace leaders will get stuck explaining to executives why their fancy AI pilot crashed into compliance issues, security problems, or worse, actually made work harder instead of easier. Here's the truth: being "ready" for AI doesn't mean buying the shiniest tools; it means having people who understand your actual workflows, your real risks, and your genuine bottlenecks before you let the algorithms loose.

industry-news.title: How to develop high-potential employees
industry-news.excerpt: Why do high-potential programs fail? It starts with strong individual performance. Find out how.
industry-news.dwp_take: HR Dive ran a piece on why high-potential employee development programs tank, with the basic insight that strong individual performance is actually where it starts. This matters to digital workplace teams because your best technical talent is probably being poached by other departments or companies if you're not actively developing them, and losing institutional knowledge hurts your ability to support the rest of the organization. Here's the thing though: most companies nail the identification part and then do nothing, leaving these people to figure out their own career path while wondering why they bother staying around.

industry-news.title: Auracast Is The Next WiFi
industry-news.excerpt: Auracast is emerging as the next generation of audio infrastructure, reshaping workplaces, hotels, retail, and public spaces much like WiFi transformed connectivity.
industry-news.dwp_take: Bluetooth's new Auracast technology allows devices to broadcast audio to multiple receivers simultaneously without pairing, creating a shared audio experience in physical spaces. For digital workplace pros, this means rethinking how conference rooms, cafeterias, and collaboration spaces handle sound and accessibility, especially for hybrid work scenarios. Look, calling it "the next WiFi" is lazy Forbes talk, but the real value is probably in accessible meetings and reducing the audio chaos of modern offices, not hype.
